text: My main symptom is Continuous heart murmur. I also have Bluish macules on the skin that do not blanch with pressure, Cloudy lenses in both eyes noticed upon examination, Failure to pass auditory screening tests.

text: The combination of a continuous heart murmur, congenital cataracts, and sensorineural hearing loss is highly suggestive of congenital rubella syndrome. REQUEST TEST: Rubella_IgG_Antibodies

speaker: Doctor
text: The negative Toxoplasma IgM result effectively rules out congenital toxoplasmosis, leaving congenital rubella syndrome as the most likely diagnosis despite the ambiguous serology, given the classic triad of cataracts, heart defect, and deafness. speaker: Doctor
text: Given the classic triad of congenital cataracts, patent ductus arteriosus (continuous murmur), and sensorineural hearing loss, congenital rubella syndrome remains the most likely diagnosis despite the negative initial serology, which can occur if maternal antibodies are still present or testing was mistimed.
